- Assignment ask is higher than our standard license approach. We usually offer a perpetual, non-exclusive license for output and commercial use but do not assign title.
- Training exclusion is reasonable as a carveout request; we can propose an explicit "no training" clause for the customer's data and offer a paid training addendum (with evidentiary attestation and SOC controls) as an opt-in.

Questions for internal alignment (can reply inline):
- Can Legal draft a narrow license that gives BoltSoft the right to commercialize Customer Output produced by our service but stops short of assignment? (Ben, Laura)
- What evidence package can Infra/OPS produce to show data segregation and that model training pipelines are gated? We should provide a checklist BoltSoft can use to confirm controls.

Suggested next steps:
1) Propose counter language replacing "assignment" with "exclusive licensed rights to Customer Output for their product lines" or similar.
2) Offer a training addendum that requires signed opt-in and a 30-day notice window, plus a SOC-2 attestation excerpt and a brief evidence checklist.
3) Quick sync with Sales + Legal before sending the counter (I can host with BoltSoft if needed).

Attachments: evidence-checklist-template.xlsx (draft).

-Kim

We should hold firm and offer a tailored exclusive license restricted to BoltSoft's specific product lines for a defined term.

- Ops/Infra evidence: we can provide the following within 48 hours:
  * Architecture diagram showing separate customer VPCs/tenancy layers (screenshot + blurb)
  * Snapshot of KV cache separation and request routing policy (short paragraph)
  * Excerpt from our internal runbook that shows gating steps before model retraining (who, approvals, audit log examples)

- Training addendum: acceptable, but product should propose pricing band (one-time fee for model access + monthly auditing fee) so legal/procurement see a commercial alternative.

Laura — can Legal prepare two clear options: (A) strongly-worded license (no assignment) + training addendum opt-in; (B) if they insist on "assignment", require a scoped carveout + compensation and full indemnity. We should surface both to procurement so they pick.

I can assemble the Ops artifacts. Laura, can you draft those two options and a suggested paragraph for the order form?

Oliver / BoltSoft team —

Thanks for the clear redlines and deadline. We reviewed internally and can propose the following compromise to move procurement forward this month:

1) Customer Output: instead of assignment, Redwood will grant BoltSoft a world-wide, perpetual, royalty-free, exclusive license to Customer Output generated via BoltSoft's use of the service for the specific product lines identified in the Order Form (we will include product-line definitions in an exhibit). This preserves control of underlying model IP while giving BoltSoft the commercial certainty they want.

2) Training / Data use: Redwood will add a "No Training Without Consent" clause to the MSA. By default Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train or improve models. If BoltSoft opts into training, that will be governed by a separate Training Addendum (attached draft) that includes:
   - Scope of data used
   - Auditability requirements and evidence we will provide
   - Commercial terms (one-time onboarding fee + monthly monitoring fee)

3) Evidence package: we are attaching an evidence-checklist-template.xlsx and can provide the following artifacts on request (redacted/snapshot forms):
   - Tenancy diagram and brief ops write-up
   - Sample audit logs showing gating approvals for retraining
   - SOC 2 summary page and point of contact for attestation verification

4) If BoltSoft insists on assignment language, Redwood requests an alternative: a time-limited exclusive license + transfer compensation and a mutual indemnity carveout for pre-existing third-party components.

Please see the attached revised MSA pages with our suggested replacement language (we will upload a tracked PDF to the Drive). If this aligns, Kim and I can hop on a 30-minute call with Procurement tomorrow to finalize.

Oliver — are you available 09:00–11:00 PT tomorrow for a short sync?
